keyAndScale.primaryKey: E major with heavy use of E power chord (E5) as the tonal center

scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - B - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Main riff motif and guitar solo; the blues-inflected minor pentatonic over a major key center creates the gritty hard rock sound

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Chorus melody and chord movement; the flatted 7th (D) is central to the E-A-B power chord progression

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Mixolydian / Blues-rock hybrid with dominant chord feel throughout
keyAndScale.keySignature: 4 sharps (F#, C#, G#, D#) nominally, but the song leans heavily on blues-based tonality
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor of E major

mainProgression.description: The iconic opening riff is built entirely on the E power chord with a chromatic walk-up from E5 to E5/F# to G5, creating the proto-metal sound that coined the term 'heavy metal' in popular music.

sectionProgressions.description: The signature chromatic walk-up riff from E to G power chords, played with heavy distortion and aggressive picking
Verse stays rooted on the E power chord with the riff motif repeating underneath the vocal melody
Classic I-IV-I-V rock progression opening up from the riff-based verse into full chords for the anthemic chorus

harmonicFunction: E5 (I) - Tonic power chord providing the heavy, driving root of the song
G5 (bIII) - Chromatic passing chord in the riff creating bluesy tension
A (IV) - Subdominant adding lift and energy in the chorus
B (V) - Dominant chord providing resolution tension in the chorus turnaround

techniques.name: Power Chord Riff with Chromatic Walk-Up
techniques.description: The signature Born to Be Wild riff using E5 power chord with a chromatic ascending line from E through F# to G, creating the proto-metal sound

notes: E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (open E power chord)
F#5: 2-4-4-X-X-X (barre power chord shape)
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (barre power chord shape)
The riff walks chromatically E-F#-G then resolves back to E
Use all downstrokes for maximum aggression at 148 BPM
Palm mute lightly between chord hits for rhythmic punch
sequence: Strike the open E5 power chord with a firm downstroke
Slide up chromatically to F#5 at the 2nd fret
Continue up to G5 at the 3rd fret
Resolve back down to the open E5 with emphasis
Repeat the riff pattern throughout intro and verses
tips: Keep your picking hand locked into steady downstrokes for the driving feel
Use slight palm muting on the E string for tightness between chord strikes
The chromatic walk-up should be smooth and even - do not rush the F# passing tone
Let the G5 ring slightly longer before resolving to E5 for dramatic effect
details.progression: E5 - F#5 - G5 - E5 (chromatic walk-up riff)

techniques.name: Open Chord Strumming (Chorus)
techniques.description: Full open chord strumming for the anthemic chorus section using standard E, A, and B chords in a I-IV-V progression

notes: E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (standard open E major)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (standard open A major)
B: X-2-4-4-4-2 (barre chord) or B7: X-2-1-2-0-2 (open voicing alternative)
Strum with full aggressive downstrokes on the beat
The chorus opens up harmonically from the tight riff into wide open chords
sequence: Transition from the E5 riff to a full open E major chord
Strum E major for two bars
Move to A major for two bars
Return to E major for two bars
Hit B (or B7) for the turnaround back to the riff
tips: The transition from power chord riff to open chords should feel like the song opening up
Strum harder and fuller during the chorus for dynamic contrast
If B barre chord is too difficult, substitute B7 open voicing
Accentuate beat 1 of each chord change to drive the rhythm forward
details.progression: E - A - E - B (I - IV - I - V)

techniques.name: Palm-Muted Power Chord Rhythm
techniques.description: Tight palm-muted chugging on the low E string between riff hits, creating the driving rhythmic foundation of the verses

notes: Rest the edge of your picking hand lightly on the strings near the bridge
Chug on the open low E string with steady eighth notes
Lift palm mute when striking the full E5 power chord for accent
The contrast between muted chugging and open chord strikes creates rhythmic dynamics
sequence: Palm mute the low E string with steady eighth-note downstrokes
Lift the palm mute on the accented E5 chord hits
Resume palm muting for the connecting rhythmic sections
Coordinate the palm mute release with the chromatic walk-up
tips: Light palm muting - you want a chunky tone, not completely dead strings
Keep the muting hand position consistent for even tone
Practice alternating between muted and open sounds at slow tempo first
This technique is fundamental to all hard rock and metal rhythm guitar

sections.name: Intro / Main Riff
sections.technique: Power Chord Riff with Chromatic Walk-Up
sections.description: The iconic opening riff that defined an era - the chromatic E5 walk-up that first put the iconic vocal hook into rock and roll
notes: All downstrokes for maximum power and drive
The chromatic walk-up E-F#-G is the signature motif
Add slight palm muting between chord strikes for rhythmic definition
Tempo is aggressive at 148 BPM - keep it tight and driving

sections.name: Verse
sections.technique: Power Chord Riff with Chromatic Walk-Up
sections.description: The verse continues the main riff underneath the vocals, maintaining the driving energy with the E5 based power chord pattern
notes: Same riff pattern continues under the verse vocal melody
Maintain consistent picking intensity throughout
The vocal rhythm follows the guitar riff closely
Slight dynamic control - not quite as loud as the intro for vocal clarity

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The anthemic chorus opens up with full chord strumming - the iconic vocal hook with a classic I-IV-V rock progression
notes: Open up from power chords to full open chord voicings
Strum with full aggression - this is the payoff moment
Strong accent on beat 1 of each chord change
The B chord resolves back to the main riff for the next verse

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Guitar solo over the riff and chorus progression, featuring blues-rock bends and pentatonic licks in E minor pentatonic
sections.progression: E5 riff - A - E - B (solo over both sections)
notes: Solo uses E minor pentatonic scale (E-G-A-B-D) at the 12th position
Aggressive string bends on the B and high E strings
Mix of pentatonic runs and sustained bends for expression
Rhythm guitar continues the main riff underneath the solo

sections.name: Outro
sections.technique: Power Chord Riff with Chromatic Walk-Up
sections.description: Final chorus repetitions building to the climactic ending with the main riff driving to a big E chord finish
sections.progression: E - A - E5 riff to end
notes: Final chorus repeats with maximum intensity
Returns to the main riff for the closing section
Big sustained E chord to finish
Let the final E ring out with full volume and sustain

guitar.recommended: Gibson SG Standard or similar dual-humbucker guitar
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for the thick, aggressive power chord tone

amp.recommended: Fender Bassman or similar vintage tube amp cranked to natural breakup
alternatives: Any tube amp with natural overdrive

effects.distortion: Cranked amp natural overdrive - no pedals on the original recording. A tube screamer or light overdrive pedal can approximate the tone at lower volumes.
effects.reverb: Light spring reverb from the amp
effects.other: No effects pedals needed. The tone comes from cranking a tube amp for natural distortion.

beginner.focus: Learn the main power chord riff and basic E-A-B chord shapes
steps: Master the open E5 power chord shape (0-2-2-X-X-X)
Practice the chromatic walk-up: E5 to F#5 to G5
Learn the basic E, A, and B (or B7) open chord shapes for the chorus
Play the riff at slow tempo with a metronome, gradually building to 148 BPM
beginner.timeEstimate: 1-2 weeks for the riff and basic structure

intermediate.focus: Add palm muting, full song structure, and tonal dynamics
steps: Add palm muting technique between power chord strikes
Practice transitioning between the riff sections and open chord chorus
Work on dynamic contrast between verse (tight riff) and chorus (open chords)
Play through the complete song structure with correct timing and feel
intermediate.timeEstimate: 2-3 weeks for confident full song performance

advanced.focus: Learn the guitar solo and refine the authentic distorted tone
steps: Learn the E minor pentatonic scale at the 12th position for the solo
Practice string bends and vibrato for expressive solo phrasing
Work on the solo note-for-note or develop your own improvisation over the changes
Dial in an authentic late-1960s cranked amp tone
advanced.timeEstimate: 3-5 weeks for complete performance with solo

commonMistakes: Using upstrokes on the riff - this song demands all downstrokes for the right feel
Rushing the chromatic walk-up - keep each note even and rhythmic
Not muting unused strings, causing unwanted noise on distorted power chords
Playing the chorus chords too quietly - the chorus should be the loudest, most open section
practiceRoutine: Warm up with open E5 power chord strikes, focusing on clean attack (3 minutes)
Practice the chromatic walk-up riff slowly, then build speed (5 minutes)
Work on transitions between power chord riff and open chorus chords (5 minutes)
Play through the full song structure at tempo with a backing track (5 minutes)
Practice palm muting technique for tightness and rhythmic control (3 minutes)
focusAreas: Clean power chord execution with proper string muting
Smooth transitions between riff sections and chorus
Dynamic contrast between tight verse riff and open chorus strumming
metronomeWork: Start the riff at 100 BPM with all downstrokes
Increase by 10 BPM increments until reaching 148 BPM
Practice the chorus chord changes at half tempo, then build up
Use metronome clicks on beats 2 and 4 for a rock backbeat feel
